explanation: Expresses purpose in a formal, written style -- 'in order to ~'.
example_sentence: 問題を解決すべく、会議が開かれた。(A meeting was held in order to solve the problem.)
drill_sentence: 夢を叶える___、彼は努力を続けた。(べく)

explanation: A literary expression of strong purpose -- 'in order to ~' (archaic-flavored).
example_sentence: 生きんがために、彼は必死に働いた。(In order to survive, he worked desperately.)
drill_sentence: 目的を達成せ___がために、全力を尽くした。(ん)

explanation: Expresses that something is entirely composed of one thing -- 'nothing but ~ / all ~'.
example_sentence: 今年はいいことずくめだった。(This year was nothing but good things.)
drill_sentence: 彼は黒___の服を着ている。(ずくめ)

explanation: Expresses that something is uniquely possible because of a specific person or place -- 'only possible because of ~'.
example_sentence: これは職人ならではの技術だ。(This is a skill only possible because of a craftsman.)
drill_sentence: この味は老舗___の味だ。(ならでは)

explanation: Expresses total denial, even of a tiny amount -- 'not even ~' (used with 一 + counter).
example_sentence: 一秒たりとも無駄にできない。(I can't waste even a single second.)
drill_sentence: 一円___無駄にしない。(たりとも)

explanation: Expresses 'whether it be ~ or ~'.
example_sentence: 晴れであれ雨であれ、試合は行われる。(Whether it's sunny or rainy, the match will be held.)
drill_sentence: 大人___あれ子供___あれ、ルールは同じだ。(で／で)

explanation: Expresses that one factor combines with another to produce an effect -- 'combined with ~'.
example_sentence: 美しい景色と相まって、旅行はより楽しいものになった。(Combined with the beautiful scenery, the trip became even more enjoyable.)
drill_sentence: 円安が好景気___相まって、輸出が伸びた。(と)

explanation: Expresses a slightly negative tendency -- 'tend to have a bad tendency to ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は物事を大げさに言うきらいがある。(He tends to exaggerate things.)
drill_sentence: 最近の若者は諦めが早い___がある。(きらい)

explanation: Expresses sufficiency for something -- 'worthy of ~ / enough to ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は信頼するに足る人物だ。(He is a person worthy of trust.)
drill_sentence: 満足する___足る結果が出た。(に)

explanation: Expresses that something is not difficult to imagine or understand -- 'not difficult to ~'.
example_sentence: 彼の悔しさは想像に難くない。(His frustration is not difficult to imagine.)
drill_sentence: 苦労は察する___難くない。(に)

explanation: Expresses that one cannot suppress a strong emotion -- 'cannot help but feel ~' (formal).
example_sentence: その事故のニュースには、驚きを禁じ得なかった。(I couldn't help but feel shocked at the news of that accident.)
drill_sentence: 彼の勇気に感動___禁じ得ない。(を)

explanation: A formal way to state a judgment or inference -- 'it is thought that ~'.
example_sentence: この状況は今後も続くものと思われる。(This situation is thought to continue in the future as well.)
drill_sentence: 原因は人的ミスである___と思われる。(もの)

explanation: A formal way to say 'without ~'.
example_sentence: 許可なしに、この部屋に入ってはいけない。(You may not enter this room without permission.)
drill_sentence: 努力___なしには、結果はついてこない。(が)

explanation: Expresses that once something happens, an inevitable result follows -- 'once ~, that's it / inevitably ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は始めたが最後、最後までやり通す。(Once he starts something, he sees it through to the end.)
drill_sentence: この扉を閉めた___最後、二度と開かない。(が)

explanation: Expresses missing the chance to do something -- 'miss the chance to ~'.
example_sentence: 忙しくて、電話をかけそびれた。(I was busy and missed the chance to call.)
drill_sentence: タイミングを逃して、言い___た。(そびれ)

explanation: Expresses being covered in something, usually dirty -- 'covered in ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は汗まみれになって働いた。(He worked while covered in sweat.)
drill_sentence: 子供は泥___になって遊んでいた。(まみれ)

explanation: Expresses that something ended without ever being done -- 'end up not doing ~'.
example_sentence: 結局、彼には会えずじまいだった。(In the end, I ended up not being able to meet him.)
drill_sentence: 本を買ったが、読ま___だった。(ずじまい)

explanation: Expresses a noticeable change that has continued ever since a certain point -- 'ever since ~'.
example_sentence: 結婚してからというもの、彼は落ち着いた。(Ever since he got married, he has settled down.)
drill_sentence: 引っ越し___からというもの、忙しい毎日が続いている。(して)

explanation: Expresses that once a situation reaches a certain level, a natural consequence follows -- 'once it becomes ~ / when it's a matter of ~'.
example_sentence: 受験生ともなると、遊ぶ時間もなくなる。(Once you become an exam candidate, you don't even have time to play.)
drill_sentence: 社長___もなると、責任も重くなる。(と)

explanation: Expresses being right at the edge or verge of a point in time -- 'just before ~ / on the verge of ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は死にぎわに、家族への感謝を語った。(On the verge of death, he spoke of his gratitude to his family.)
drill_sentence: 別れ___に、彼女は涙を見せた。(ぎわ)

explanation: Expresses that one case would be acceptable, but another is not -- 'if it were just ~, that would be one thing, but ~'.
example_sentence: 一回ならまだしも、三回も遅刻するのはひどい。(If it were just once, that'd be one thing, but being late three times is terrible.)
drill_sentence: 知らない___まだしも、知っていて黙っていたのは問題だ。(なら)

explanation: Emphasizes an extreme case -- 'even ~ / just ~' (formal, often with negative predicates).
example_sentence: 想像だに恐ろしい。(It's frightening even to imagine.)
drill_sentence: 考える___恐ろしい結果だ。(だに)

explanation: Expresses being the best within a certain group -- 'the leading ~ of ~'.
example_sentence: 彼は社内きっての営業マンだ。(He is the best salesman in the company.)
drill_sentence: 彼女はこの町___の美人だ。(きって)

explanation: Expresses that something exists only thanks to another thing -- 'only possible because of ~ / thanks to ~'.
example_sentence: ファンあっての芸能人だ。(An entertainer exists only because of their fans.)
drill_sentence: 健康___の人生だ。(あって)

explanation: Expresses that someone's attitude conveys an unspoken message -- 'as if to say ~'.
example_sentence: 彼はもう帰れと言わんばかりに、時計を見た。(He looked at the clock as if to say 'go home already'.)
drill_sentence: 彼女は興味がない___言わんばかりに、目をそらした。(と)

explanation: A formal, somewhat archaic way to give a reason, often as an excuse -- 'since ~ / because ~'.
example_sentence: 慣れぬこととて、失礼があったかもしれません。(Since I'm not used to this, I may have been rude.)
drill_sentence: 初めての___とて、うまくできませんでした。(こと)

explanation: Expresses that something is unbearable to experience, or (with certain nouns) a deep feeling -- 'cannot bear to ~ / deeply ~'.
example_sentence: 見るにたえない光景だった。(It was a sight unbearable to watch.)
drill_sentence: 彼の行為は遺憾___たえない。(に)

explanation: Expresses a weak possibility -- 'it's not that ~ isn't possible / it could happen'.
example_sentence: 条件次第では、協力しないものでもない。(Depending on the conditions, it's not impossible that I'd cooperate.)
drill_sentence: 頼まれれば、引き受け___でもない。(ないもの)

explanation: A formal attributive form of べからず, modifying a noun -- '~ that must not be ~'.
example_sentence: これは許すべからざる行為だ。(This is an act that must not be forgiven.)
drill_sentence: 彼の発言は看過す___行為だ。(べからざる)

pattern: 〜いかんによらず／〜いかんにかかわらず
explanation: Expresses 'regardless of ~ / no matter what ~ is'.
example_sentence: 理由のいかんによらず、遅刻は遅刻だ。(Regardless of the reason, being late is being late.)
drill_sentence: 結果の___によらず、最善を尽くします。(いかん)
